TASK ID: independent-set-to-vertex-cover

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Independent Set to Vertex Cover. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Independent Set and TARGET is Vertex Cover. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = IndependentSet
Independent Set.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has an independent set of AT LEAST k vertices: k
vertices with no edge between any two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k > n is always no. With no edges,
every set of vertices is independent.

TARGET = VertexCover
Vertex Cover.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a vertex cover of AT MOST k vertices: a set of
vertices that includes at least one endpoint of every edge.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. A graph with no edges is yes for every
k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
every edge.

WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-cpqowl5o

    reduce(instance) -> instance
It takes an instance of the source problem and returns an instance of the target problem, both in the formats documented in problems.py. The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

Before submitting, check your reduction. problems.py has no solvers, so first write your own brute-force solvers for both problems from the definitions above. Then write tests in test_reduce.py that compare your solvers' answers on many small source instances and their reductions, run them, and revise until the tests pass. {"command":"cd /tmp/reduction-cpqowl5o && cat > reduce.py <<'EOF'
"""Polynomial-time reduction from Independent Set to Vertex Cover.

A set S is an independent set in G = (V, E) if and only if its complement
V \ S is a vertex cover of G.  Therefore G has an independent set of size
at least k exactly when G has a vertex cover of size at most n - k.

The reduction keeps the graph unchanged and maps the parameter k to n - k.
This is computable in O(|V| + |E|) time (polynomial).
"""

from __future__ import annotations
